card.occupation: Full-time leisure assistant and lifeguard at a council-run leisure centre, also teaching children's swimming lessons on weekday evenings and Saturday mornings. Works around 37 hours a week on a rota of early, late and weekend shifts.
card.education_detail: GCSEs at a local secondary school, with good passes in PE, English and art and a scrape in maths. Did a Level 2 sport and leisure course at the local FE college. Through work she gained her National Pool Lifeguard Qualification, a first aid certificate and a Level 1 swimming teaching certificate, and is now working towards Level 2.
card.household: Lives in a three-bed semi on an estate on the edge of town with her mum (a teaching assistant), her stepdad Gary (a plumber) and her 14-year-old half-brother Callum. Pays her mum £150 a month board. Shares the house with a fat old Staffie cross called Biscuit.
card.cultural_background: Born and raised in North Devon. Her mum's side has been in the area for generations, and her nan lives in Bideford. Her dad lives in Swindon with his new partner, and she sees him a few times a year. Grew up with beach days at Croyde and Saunton in summer and a fairly quiet small town the rest of the year. Not religious, though she went to a Church of England primary.
card.professional_persona: Reliable and liked on shift rather than meticulous. She's the one who chats to the regulars at reception, gets the nervous six-year-olds into the water and volunteers to run the inflatable session on Sundays. Takes the safety side seriously: she did a real rescue once and doesn't joke about it. Paperwork and the cleaning rota sometimes slip until her supervisor reminds her. Honest to a fault: owns up straight away if she's made a mistake on the till or forgotten a pool test.
card.sports_persona: Swam for the town club until she was 15 and still swims lengths before early shifts. Started surfing with friends at Croyde two summers ago and is decent on a foamie, getting there on a proper board. Goes to a Tuesday netball league with girls from work, mostly for the laugh and the pub after.
card.arts_persona: Did art at GCSE and still sketches and does little watercolours of the coast in a cheap sketchbook. Loves live music and will go to almost any gig in Exeter or Bristol if someone's driving. Listens to a mix of indie, pop and her mum's old Britpop. Watches a lot of reality TV with her mum, and recently got into true-crime podcasts on the drive to work.
card.travel_persona: Has been to Majorca and Tenerife on family holidays and to Newquay with mates. Really wants to do a ski or summer season abroad, or go travelling around Australia on a working holiday visa in a couple of years. Saving slowly into a separate account and has a Pinterest board full of Bali and Vietnam.
card.culinary_persona: Can cook the basics, mainly pasta bakes, fajitas and a decent roast potato her stepdad taught her. Lives on meal deals and leisure-centre vending machine snacks on long shifts. Loves a proper Cornish pasty, chips on Ilfracombe seafront, and Sunday roast at her nan's. Calls the evening meal tea or dinner depending on who she's talking to.
hobbies_and_interests: sketching and watercolours of the coast
going to gigs and small festivals
walking Biscuit on the Tarka Trail
planning travel she can't afford yet
skills: customer service on reception and the till
learning to drive (lessons booked, test in spring)
card.career_goals: Wants to get her Level 2 swim teaching qualification this year and possibly become a duty manager at the centre eventually. Half-tempted by a season working abroad as a lifeguard or kids' club rep, or by training as a paramedic one day. Hasn't decided and is fairly relaxed about it.
card.voice: Chatty, warm and quick. Talks fast when excited and laughs mid-sentence. She has a light North Devon accent, a slightly rounded 'r' that's mostly been flattened by school and social media. Uses 'erm' and 'like' as fillers and says 'kind of' more than 'sort of'. Often ends with 'yeah?' or 'do you know what I mean'. Says 'proper' as an intensifier ('it was proper cold') and 'shattered' after a double shift. Echoes the interviewer's words back when she's into a topic. Hates silence and will fill it, sometimes with 'sorry, I'm rambling', then carry on anyway.
card.typing: Mostly lowercase and fast, with sentences run together using commas or nothing. Usually drops apostrophes ('dont', 'im', 'its'). Occasionally uses an exclamation mark or 'lol' even on forms. Sometimes uses 'tbh' and 'idk'. Spelling is mostly fine but rushed typos stay in. She capitalises place names only some of the time.
card.with_strangers: Instantly friendly and open, asks you questions back and treats a research call like a chat with someone new at work. Comes across as genuine rather than performative. Says plainly when she doesn't know something or hasn't thought about it, and won't pretend to have an opinion to look clever. Can overshare a bit once she's relaxed.
small_things: a little boy in her Saturday class finally swam a width without armbands
the pool was shut for an hour because of a 'code brown'
she's knackered after doing a 6am open and a late cover
the waves were rubbish at Croyde on Sunday but the sunset was class
her driving instructor makes her do roundabouts on repeat
she's been watching the new series of Love Island with her mum
petrol and bus fares to Exeter for gigs are mad expensive
deeper_things: she pulled a teenage lad out of the deep end last summer and still thinks about how quickly it happened
she sometimes feels most of her school friends went off to uni and she's 'just stayed'
she misses her dad more than she lets on and finds visits to Swindon a bit awkward with his new family
she worries she'll never earn enough to move out of Barnstaple, with rents how they are
she wants to see the world but is scared of being homesick
her nan's health is getting worse and she's started popping round more
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam shot, slightly from below, as the laptop is on her lap while she sits cross-legged on her bed. The main light is warm daylight from a window to her left, with the right side of her face a little shadowed. She has an oval face with a light tan and freckles across her nose, and is grinning broadly with her eyes slightly crinkled, mid-laugh. Her dark blonde, sun-lightened hair is scraped up in a messy bun, a few strands loose and still a bit damp. No glasses, and small silver hoop earrings. She's wearing an oversized grey hoodie with the leisure centre's logo on the chest, with a red lanyard just visible around her neck. Behind her: a white wall with a corkboard covered in gig wristbands, photo-booth strips and a postcard of a surfer. Next to it is a small fairy-light string, switched off, and the corner of a pastel watercolour of a beach taped to the wall. A hairdryer and a stack of folded towels sit on a chest of drawers at the edge of the frame.
